refamilied.why: T-1681, piece 2 of 4 of T-1201, and it re-families three slots this block already built rather than dealing it any new ground. THE GROUND IS THE FINDING, exactly as it was on T-1647's block. Both of the blocks this piece owns read at_capacity in the 665-roof programme -- blk_lake_clark 16 standing roofs and blk_lake_dearborn 13, headroom 0 on each -- and blk_lake_clark's one remaining free lot is lot 5, on Randolph, which this parcel's own end rule keeps open. So what the Lake business front is MADE OF can only change by saying what the roofs already standing on it are. WHAT IS WRONG TODAY, MEASURED ON THE COMMITTED TREE. The Lake faces of these two blocks -- lots 0, 2, 4 and 6 of each, every one of them fronting a street this project's own hierarchy grades `principal` -- carried 15 principal roofs between them, and 4 of those were store or workshop families, against the 0.6818 documented trade share T-0213 reads off a principal street (1835_665_roof_programme.json, method.business_front.trade_share_by_class). This block's own Lake face carried nine principal roofs, three of them stores; the three units of the party-line run on lot 0 were an older log cabin and two frame cottages, and the street-face register had a documented Lake Street trade seated in every one of them. A documented business standing in a cottage's silhouette on a principal street is the reconstruction contradicting its own business layer, and nothing about the buildings is evidence: all three are anonymous count-units whose family was picked off this block's scheduled mix, and the schedule apportions the family, never the building. WHICH THREE FAMILIES, AND WHY THEY ARE THESE THREE. C1, C2 and C3 are the three store families the 665-roof programme still has headroom for in the south division -- 17 of 18 standing, 11 of 13 and 12 of 17 -- and the run takes one of each, so the face gains three stores without any family passing its own target. C4 is refused and the refusal is the ground's: a wide two-storey mixed block bands at 28-36 ft of frontage and no unit of this run has more than 22 ft of it. WHICH ONE STANDS WHERE IS THE BLOCK'S OWN END RULE AND NOT AN ALLOCATION. T-0079 seated this run under the rule that the better roof stands at the town-centre end, which here is EAST toward Dearborn and the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835. So the run now ascends along the face: C1, the one-storey shop, on the Clark corner; C2, the storey-and-a-half store-residence, in the middle; C3, the narrow two-storey store, closing the run at the east end. That is the same ordering the cottages stood in and the same rule that put them there. IT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT ABOUT WHICH BUSINESS SITS IN WHICH ROOF, BECAUSE THAT IS NOT A READING. Street-face adoption ranks the face's documented businesses by evidence and pairs them with its free roofs IN ID ORDER, and every row it writes carries `order_is_a_claim: false`. Three ids moved here, so the Lake face's trades re-paired across it -- W. G. Blanchard, house and land agent, and G. Blanshard, houses and lots for sale or to let, now take the first two units and Dr. W. G. Austin's botanic practice the third, and Sarah D. Howe's dress and cloak making moved along the same face to recon_1835_west_007. Not one of those pairings is evidence and none of them is what chose a family. What the register does say, and what this re-family answers, is that Lake Street's own documented trade sits on this run at all. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: no roof changes lot, setback, anchor, party line or lateral offset; none is promoted (all three stay `reconstructed` anonymous count-units at the bottom tier); no occupant is invented -- each keeps whichever the business layer's own allocation gives it -- and the block is dealt no extra roof. The footprint is not authored here either: `generate_block_infill` samples a slot inside its family's own band on a stable key, so all three re-derive, and the crosswalk's `required_variant` for each family is what the archetype then draws -- the one-storey shopfront, the knee-wall attic T-1659 gave C2, and C3's full second storey. The three ids move with the family (_d1_01 -> _c1_01, _d3_02 -> _c2_02, _d5_03 -> _c3_03) and the two abutment anchors in this recipe are carried across with them. BLK_LAKE_DEARBORN MOVES NOTHING, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Its Lake face already carries the two trade roofs the evidence gives it -- dole_warehouse_south and mason_blacksmith_shop, both named and documented -- with St Mary's church on the lot 6 corner. The four anonymous roofs left on that face (recon_1835_south_d3_017, _d1_018, _d4_019 and _d6_020) carry NO occupant at all, so the test that moved the three above does not reach one of them; and none of them is this recipe's to move in any case, because all four belong to `phase1_south_mixed_blocks` and the phase-one parcel's re-family route is the adjudicated ledger at data/reconstruction/1835_roof_redeal.json, not a slot in this file. Re-familying a roof that carries no trade would be inventing the trade.

This generator authors no coordinates: every metre comes from a committed lot polygon inside a block bounded by four platted streets, and F3's own crosswalk entry requires a landing apron following site access. Sampled against the committed heightfield the nearest water to this block's boundary is 134 m away. So the slot is DEFERRED and named in `deferred` with its reason, tools/generate_block_infill.py refuses F3 by name from this run onward, and the fault is filed against the DEAL as T-0275 rather than against the block — the roof is still owed and the wharf ground is where it belongs. THE SECOND CLAUSE OF THE CORE DENSITY STANDARD IS SPENT: an improved lot carries its outbuildings, so the stable stands in lot 4's own yard at the alley end, behind the row this parcel built, which is the only lot on this block whose yard belongs to a roof this parcel owns. NO ROOF IS ADDED TO THE TOWN: the three come out of south_plat_beyond_committed_control, the district balance waiting on street control past State and Washington, and every marginal still sums to the programme total. WHAT IS UNVERIFIED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this ground, that there were two of them, that they stood shoulder to shoulder, and that the better of them stood at the east end are all inventions of this programme. No lot is numbered — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet — and the side lot line the row crosses between its own units is conjectural in every record this generator has ever written. The block face the row stands on is committed geometry derived from the street centrelines, which is the unit the standard counts in.

refamilied.why: T-1682, piece 3 of 4 of T-1201, and it re-families ONE slot this block already built rather than dealing it any new ground. THE GROUND IS THE FINDING, and it is the same one T-1647 reached on the South Water row. T-1201 asked for the Lake frontage of the Franklin, La Salle, Wells, Market and Clinton blocks to stand as stores, and there is nowhere left to raise one: every one of the seven Lake-Randolph blocks reads `at_capacity` with headroom 0 in the 665-roof programme (clinton 11 standing of 31 capacity, market 10, franklin 14, wells 14, lasalle 14, clark 16, dearborn 13), so what the Lake business front is MADE OF can only change by saying what the roofs already standing on it are. AND ONLY TWO OF THE FIVE BLOCKS HOLD A ROOF THIS PROGRAMME MAY SPEAK FOR. blk_lake_wells, blk_lake_lasalle and blk_lake_clinton carry no record this parcel authored at all - their 14, 14 and 11 standing roofs belong to the research layer and to the phase-one South parcel, and a documented building is not this programme's to re-family. That is a refusal on the committed tree and not an omission: those three blocks' Lake frontage cannot be composed by this ticket in either direction. THE CARD THAT ASKS FOR IT: seq 01, the deep-plan frame cottage anchored on the east end of this block's Lake frontage run, is William Clay - hat manufacturing and dealing, seated here by the street-face adoption policy off the Chicago Democrat. A documented hatter standing in a cottage's silhouette on the Lake Street business face is the reconstruction contradicting its own business layer, and nothing about the building is evidence: it is an anonymous count-unit whose family was picked off this block's scheduled mix, and the schedule apportions the family, never the building. WHAT IS LEFT AS IT STANDS, AND WHY: seq 02, the older log dwelling west of it, is '[uncertain: the dentist lodging near Lake Street, July 1834] - dentistry'. Dentistry is a PROFESSION practised in lodgings, not a shop with a counter, and T-1648 refused the same move on the South Water run for a workshop and a school on exactly this ground. It keeps its cabin. THE FAMILY IS THE EVIDENCE'S CHOICE AND THE CEILING IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. C2, the store-residence, is the family a trade that MANUFACTURES AND DEALS belongs to - its own crosswalk variants read 'shop below; attic rooms; rear lean-to; signboard' - and that is what this card says the keeper does. C3 and C4 are two-storey stores and nothing on this card is evidence of a second storey or of the capital one implies; dealing one to make the frontage read richer is the confidence upgrade AGENTS.md rule 2 forbids, so the store-residence is the largest store family the EVIDENCE admits here rather than the largest the metres would take. C2's 18x30-22x40 ft band overlaps D5's 18x28-24x34, so the roof does not grow past the ground its slot already stood on. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: the slot keeps its lot, setback, anchor and lateral offset, it is not promoted (it stays a `reconstructed` anonymous count-unit at the bottom tier), no occupant is invented - it keeps the one the street-face adoption policy already gave it - and the block is dealt no extra roof. The footprint is not authored here either: `generate_block_infill` samples a slot inside its family's own band on a stable key, so the record re-derives.

open_lots.why: A Washington-tier interior lot, open on the programme's own alternating-vacancy assumption since the first deal and untouched by this one. It is the lot this block keeps open now that the corner is built on, and the standard is explicit that capacity is a ceiling rather than a target.

frontage.why: T-0317, the successor T-0028's programme owes, and the first parcel in this project where the core density standard's corner clause and the end rule point in OPPOSITE directions. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py randolph washington market franklin — and on the committed dataset Randolph carries 7 documented records and 7 inferred households against Washington's 1 and 0, Market's 2 and 1, and Franklin's 2 and 1. Randolph is this block's business face by the town's own record and it is FULL: the first deal took lots 0 and 2 and the inferred-household layer's two sawyer dwellings hold 4 and 6, so every lot on that face carries a roof and the two lots this block has left are both on the Washington tier. WHAT BINDS IS THE STANDARD'S THIRD CLAUSE. Lot 1 is the block's one free CORNER lot, the south-west one, fronting Washington along its long edge and Market Street along its short one, and a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER — an east-anchored run packs back toward the middle of the face and stops wherever its roofs run out, so the corner is the one piece of frontage a row can never reach. The run is packed WEST to it. AND THE GRADING RUNS THE OTHER WAY, which is the finding here. On blk_randolph_dearborn's third deal the free corner was at Dearborn — the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — so building to the corner and standing the best roof nearest the crossing were the same act, and the parcel could not tell the two clauses apart. This corner is at MARKET, the far end of the face from that bridge, so they separate: the corner clause fixes WHERE THE ROW STANDS and the end rule fixes WHICH ROOF STANDS WHERE IN IT, and on this block they are demonstrably different questions. THE END RULE IS READ, NOT ASSERTED: tools/measure_end_rule.py reads this face at a spread of 71.03 m and a unit step of 6.07 m under the walked criterion and grades on it, while the same face under T-A11's straight line reads 4.82 m and is BELOW THE FLOOR — so the walk is what makes a grading possible here at all, and the straight line would have been grading this parcel's own declared setback invention. The row is therefore graded EAST, toward Franklin and the bridge beyond it: the meanest dwelling stands on the corner and the best closes the run at the east end. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs toward are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. The Washington face carries no committed street wall for the run to adopt — the two roofs already standing on that tier are one-per-lot placements set back inside their own lots — so this run is the first line on the face and states the margin rather than adopting one.
frontage.runs: One run of three on lot 1, anchored 1.5 m clear of the Washington-and-Market corner at the west end of the lot's own frontage and chaining EAST from it on two shared party walls. The rough plank dwelling takes the corner itself, the older log cabin stands next to it, and the deep-plan frame cottage closes the run at the east end. It occupies 16.60 m of the lot's 20.70 m of buildable frontage — the lot measures 23.70 m on the committed block boundary and the plat module's 1.5 m margin is kept clear of each of its two conjectural side lines. The ceiling the standard measures is three units to a lot and this run spends all three; the 4.10 m left over are at the EAST end, away from the corner, which is the difference between a run built to the corner and a run that merely stands on the corner lot.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE SECOND DEAL ON THIS BLOCK. The first deal (2026-08-14, the entry above) built eight roofs under the rule that allowed one principal roof per platted lot; T-0079 retired that ceiling — three party-line units per lot, measured at the smallest lot on the committed grid — and this block has stood below the new one ever since, with four roofs of headroom and two free lots. Rewriting the first entry to cover both deals would restate an August schedule under numbers that were not true in August, so the second deal is its own entry against its own headroom, numbered from `seq_start` so the two cannot collide on a record id. WHAT IS BUILT: three principal roofs shoulder to shoulder on lot 1, the block's one free corner lot, and the stable that belongs to the lot they stand on. WHY THIS BLOCK AND NOT ANOTHER: it is the only workable ground the schedule has left for this programme. No ungenerated platted block is free to open — blk_south_water_market is blocked on the owner at T-0183, where Market and South Water is a bend in Wacker Drive rather than a crossing and the node rule cannot derive a control point, and blk_south_water_clinton is `not_a_block` (T-0163). Of the blocks still `open` in the schedule, four of the five front the South Water reach whose committed street line is the open question in T-0009, and T-0143 and T-0188 both refused to tighten a row against a line that may move. That refusal still stands, and it leaves this block's second deal. THE CORNER CLAUSE AND THE END RULE COME APART HERE, and that is the parcel's one new reading: the corner is at Market, the far end of the face from the Dearborn drawbridge, so a run built to the corner is graded away from it. The frontage entry holds the measurements. THE THREE DWELLINGS ARE GRADED BY THE CROSSWALK'S OWN RANKING and not by taste: the deep-plan frame cottage is priority rank 3, the older log cabin rank 4 and the rough plank dwelling rank 7, so best to meanest is D5, D1, D2 and the run reads D2, D1, D5 from the corner eastward. THAT A LOG CABIN AND A PLANK DWELLING MAY STAND SHOULDER TO SHOULDER WITH A FRAME COTTAGE is the frontage-fabric rule this file already states, read on a back street rather than a principal one — Washington is not in the committed hierarchy's principal class, so the rule's ranking clause has nothing to bind here and the row is dealt as the schedule dealt it. LOT 1 STOPS BEING OPEN. The first deal left it open because it is the Washington-and-Market corner and Market is the river edge of the South Division here, which made it the least attractive residential lot on the block; that reading is answered rather than overturned — the run is graded so the block's meanest roof is the one that takes it — and the lot moves to the class T-0105 built for exactly this, `built on by another deal on this block`, because the lot-accounting gate refuses a lot that is called open and built on at once. LOT 5 STAYS OPEN and the block is not built out: capacity is a ceiling rather than a target, and a block whose every lot is built is a claim nobody made. NO ROOF IS ADDED TO THE TOWN — the four come out of south_plat_beyond_committed_control, the south district's balance waiting on street control past State and Washington, and every marginal still sums to the programme's total. WHAT IS UNVERIFIED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this ground, that there were three of them, that they stood shoulder to shoulder, and that the meanest of them took the corner are all inventions of this programme. The side lot lines the row crosses between its own units are conjectural in every record this generator has ever written; the block face it stands on is committed geometry derived from the street centrelines, which is the unit the standard counts in.

frontage.why: T-0429, and the ground it stands on was unblocked by an owner's ruling rather than found. T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might move, and T-0317 inherited the refusal; T-0009 closed it on 2026-08-29 under the owner's ruling that THE DRAWN SOUTH WATER LINE DOES NOT MOVE — the corridor was re-derived from committed control and data/streets/1835.json was not touched. That refusal is what had held this reach, and it is discharged. THE FACE IS THE BLOCK'S OWN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: tools/measure_street_frontage.py reads South Water and Lake as the two faces of this block, the committed street hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades both `principal`, and South Water is the river street the owner's reference plate draws — 'South Water Street in 1834', roughly ten one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river. This run is the west half of that row on this block. THE LINE IS NOT AUTHORED AT ALL, which is the difference between this run and the first deal's: the face is already built, so the run declares `adopts_face_line` and the 1.5 m is MEASURED off the three units the first deal stands on the same face — 1.4998, 1.4996 and 1.5004 m, a 0.8 mm spread — under T-0104's clause. A street wall is one wall, and this row joins one rather than opening one. THE CORNER CLAUSE BINDS AND THE FABRIC RULE AGREES WITH IT, which is the parcel's one new reading. Lot 0 is the block's free CORNER lot, at South Water and LaSalle, and the core density standard's third clause says a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER: the run is anchored WEST, 1.5 m clear of the corner margin, and chains east on shared party walls. The frontage-fabric rule (T-0022) independently says a log dwelling takes the WEST END of a principal-street row where the block was dealt one, and this block was dealt a D1. On blk_randolph_market (T-0317) the corner clause and the end rule pointed in opposite directions and the parcel had to choose; here the corner clause and the fabric rule name the SAME unit, so the log cabin takes the corner and nothing has to be traded away. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the strip's two ends and the party walls between units are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the lots this run was dealt are named here so the ledger can count them rather than shared out one per unit.
frontage.runs: One run of six on lots 0 and 2, anchored 1.5 m clear of the South Water and LaSalle corner at the west end of lot 0's own frontage and chaining EAST from it on five shared party walls. The older log cabin takes the corner itself; the rough plank dwelling, the one-room frame cottage, the one-and-a-half-storey cottage and the small two-storey frame house follow it eastward in that order; the narrow two-storey store closes the run. It occupies 34.88 m of the strip's 47.20 m of buildable frontage — the two lots measure 50.20 m end to end on the committed block boundary and the plat module's 1.5 m margin is kept clear at each end. The ceiling the standard measures is three units to a lot and this run spends all six it is entitled to. The 12.32 m left over are at the EAST end, between this run and the first deal's, which begins 6.84 m further east again at 54.90 m: that gap is frontage this parcel was not dealt, not a hole in a row, and a run is one continuous stretch of wall while the ground between two runs is neither's.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE SECOND DEAL ON THIS BLOCK, and the first of the four South Water blocks T-0009 unblocked (T-0429, from T-0420). WHAT IS BUILT: six principal roofs shoulder to shoulder along the whole west half of this block's river frontage — the longest single party-line run this programme has built — and the two yard buildings that belong to the lots they stand on. WHY THIS BLOCK COULD NOT BE DEALT UNTIL NOW, and there were two reasons rather than one. The first is the street line: T-0143 and T-0188 refused to tighten a row against a line that might move and T-0317 inherited the refusal, until T-0009 ruled on 2026-08-29 that the drawn South Water line does not move. The second was inside this recipe and nobody had measured it — the first deal declared its run's frontage as lots 0, 2 and 4 and the run stands on lot 4 alone, so `check_block`'s lot classes read lots 0 and 2 as built on while `tools/plat_occupancy.py`, which measures footprints, read them as free and the schedule went on dealing this block eight roofs it had no declared ground for. The correction is recorded on the first entry above; it moved no roof and changed no record. THE ROW'S ORDER, and which rule fixed each part of it. The log cabin takes the west end under TWO rules that here agree: the corner clause of the core density standard (a corner lot builds to the corner, and lot 0 is this block's free corner at South Water and LaSalle) and the frontage-fabric rule of T-0022 (a log dwelling takes the west end of a principal-street row where the block was dealt one, so the row reads log and frame as the owner's plate draws it). The four dwellings east of it are graded by the END RULE under its committed criterion, the WALK to the Dearborn Street drawbridge along the committed centrelines: worst to best running east, the rough plank dwelling, the one-room frame cottage, the one-and-a-half-storey cottage and the small two-storey frame house, which is also the order of their own storeys and footprint bands in the crosswalk rather than a taste. NO SOURCE SAYS ANY OF THIS and every record repeats so in its own position note. THE STORE IS NOT IN THAT GRADING, because T-0024 settled that the face rule ranks dwellings and a non-dwelling is placed by its FUNCTION: it takes the block's better face, which the committed hierarchy grades `principal` on this side, and it stands ON the street line rather than back at a dwelling's setback, which the whole run does. Its place at the east end of the run is the functional half of the same clause — it is the end of the block a stranger reaches first coming from the town centre at Clark and the Dearborn crossing beyond it, which is the direction this block's first deal already named. THE TWO YARD BUILDINGS serve the two lots the run stands on and no others: the stable in lot 0's yard at the alley, the barn or carriage shed in lot 2's, on opposite sides of their lots so they share no alley frontage. LOT 1 STAYS OPEN and this block does not reach capacity. NO ROOF IS ADDED TO THE TOWN: the eight come out of `south_plat_beyond_committed_control`, the south district's balance waiting on street control, and every marginal still sums to the programme's total. WHAT IS UNVERIFIED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this ground, that there were six of them, that they stood shoulder to shoulder, that a store closed the run and that a log cabin took the corner are all inventions of this programme. The side lot lines the row crosses between its own units are conjectural in every record this generator has ever written; the block face it stands on is committed geometry derived from the street centrelines, which is the unit the standard counts in.

withdrawn_open_lots.why: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-06 (T-0783), AND THE LOT IS NOT OPEN ANY MORE. This entry read the Lake-and-LaSalle corner as the block's least attractive residential lot - Lake is this block's back street and LaSalle the end running west toward the lumber yards and the wharves - and left it open on that reading plus the density standard's clause that capacity is a ceiling and not a target. Neither half of that is retracted: the reading is still why the anonymous programme dealt this corner nothing, and it is a judgement about where a reconstruction should INVENT a house. What has changed is that this corner is no longer a question for the programme to answer. The Chicago Democrat of 21 May 1834 offers for sale 'the House on [the corner] of Lasalle and Lake streets', 16 by 30 feet, and `lasalle_lake_house` stands on lot 1 on that evidence. A documented building outranks an open-lot reading: the standard withholds a lot from INVENTION, not from the town. THE OTHER THREE QUARTERS OF THE CROSSING COULD NOT TAKE IT - blk_lake_lasalle lot 0 carries old_bank_building, blk_lake_wells lot 6 carries three roofs and blk_south_water_wells lot 7 one, so this was the only quarter where a documented house could stand without putting a second principal roof on a lot. This block therefore runs at capacity with no lot held open, which is a consequence of evidence arriving rather than of a deal filling the block; the density standard's clause binds the parcels and is not overturned here.

open_lots.why: The Lake-and-Franklin corner, open since the first deal and untouched by this one. Franklin is the lumber-and-wharf end of this block and Lake is its back street, so the corner where the two meet is the least attractive residential lot the block has — the reading the first deal made of it, which this deal has no cause to overturn because it was dealt no roof that wants a back-street corner. It is the lot this block keeps open, and the core density standard is explicit that capacity is a ceiling and not a target: a block whose every lot is built on is a claim about 1835 that nobody made.

frontage.why: T-0430, the second deal on this block, and the SECOND of the four South Water blocks T-0009's ruling unblocked — blk_south_water_lasalle took its own second deal first, on 2026-08-30 under T-0429, and the reading below is that run's reading applied to different ground rather than a new one. THE FACE IS NOT RE-ARGUED: this block's north face is South Water Street, the town's business front, and the committed hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades it `principal`. What was in doubt until that ruling is whether the LINE would move — T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might, and T-0317 inherited the refusal. T-0009 closed it: the corridor was re-derived from committed control (`recentred`, +8.58 m) and data/streets/1835.json was not touched, so the drawn line does not move. THE ROW STILL STANDS ON THE BLOCK FACE AND NOT ON THAT CORRIDOR, which is the distinction the two refusals were protecting: the face is committed geometry read from data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the run takes its line, its bearing and the end it packs back from off that boundary. The 8.58 m the corridor moved is therefore not in this placement at all, and if the strip between the corridor and the block faces is later resolved (T-0419) these roofs do not move with it. THE LOT IS THE ONE THE SCHEDULE COUNTS FREE, AND IT TOOK A LEDGER REPAIR TO REACH IT. tools/reconcile_665.py derives this block at 11 standing roofs, 2 free lots and 4 of headroom; the free lots are 1 and 2, read by tools/plat_occupancy.py's `exclusive_lots` from what actually stands. Lot 1 is the Lake-and-Franklin corner on the back tier and stays open. Lot 2 is this block's one free lot of business frontage — and the first entry above had RESERVED it by naming lots 2, 4 and 6 as the frontage its run was dealt, when the run it built stands on lot 6 alone. That entry now names lots 4 and 6 — lot 4 because its own privy stands in that lot's yard, lot 6 because that is where its roofs are — and lot 2, which nothing it wrote has ever stood on, comes off the list. The correction moves no record and is set out in its own `why`. THE CORNER CLAUSE DOES NOT BIND HERE and is not invoked: lot 0 is the Franklin corner and lot 6 the Wells corner, both built on, so lot 2 is an interior lot of this face and there is no corner for a run to be built to. THE END RULE IS READ RATHER THAN ASSERTED — tools/measure_end_rule.py reads this face at a spread of 73.22 m and a unit step of 6.07 m under the walked criterion, which is above the 6.00 m floor, so a grading is admissible here; the walk from lot 2's frontage to the Dearborn drawbridge's south abutment is 453.19 m against lot 4's 428.78 m and lot 6's 404.36 m, so the better end of this face, and of this lot, is the EAST. The run is anchored there and packs west. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, lot 2's own stretch of it and the end the run packs back from are all read from the committed block boundary, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. The row adopts the setback the three roofs already standing on this face were built to, so the street wall of blk_south_water_franklin stays one wall.
frontage.runs: One run of three on lot 2, anchored 1.5 m clear of the lot's east side line and chaining WEST from it on two shared party walls. The two-room frame cottage takes the east end — the end of the face nearest the Dearborn drawbridge — the deep-plan frame cottage stands next to it, and the store-residence closes the run at the west end. The ceiling the core density standard measures is three units to a lot and this run spends all three; what is left over is at the WEST end of the lot, which is where the ground is least useful to it: J. H. Kinzie's forwarding store laps this face from lot 0 and its east wall reads 23.46 m along, so a run packed the other way would have had to break around a documented store that stands proud of the platted line. Packed east, the run's west wall stands clear of that store by more than the three metres the separation gate requires and the gap between them is frontage this parcel was not dealt, not a break anybody chose — the same sentence the first deal wrote about the gap on its own side of the block, and for the same reason.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE SECOND DEAL ON THIS BLOCK, and the second of the four South Water blocks T-0365's successor split into one ticket each (T-0429..T-0432) to reach the ground; blk_south_water_lasalle was the first, and its own second deal stands committed. The first deal (2026-08-15, the entry above) built seven roofs under the rule that allowed one principal roof per platted lot; T-0079 retired that ceiling — three party-line units per lot, measured at the smallest lot on the committed grid — and this block has stood below the new one ever since, at 11 standing roofs against a capacity of 31, with two free lots and four roofs of headroom. Rewriting the first entry to cover both deals would restate an August schedule under numbers that were not true in August, so the second deal is its own entry against its own headroom, numbered from `seq_start` so the two cannot collide on a record id. WHAT IS BUILT: three principal roofs shoulder to shoulder on lot 2, this block's one free lot of South Water frontage, and the privy that belongs to the lot they stand on. WHY THIS GROUND IS WORKABLE NOW: it is the refusal T-0009 discharged. Four of the five blocks the schedule still lists `open` front this reach of South Water, and until 2026-08-29 every one of them was held by T-0143's and T-0188's refusal to tighten a row against a street line that might move. The corridor was re-derived rather than redrawn, so the line did not move and the refusal is spent. blk_south_water_market is NOT one of the four and is not in this family: T-0183 measured it as a wedge the South Branch pinches to 2.8 m of depth at Market, and what to do with that wedge is with the owner. THE THREE ROOFS ARE ORDERED BY TWO DIFFERENT RULES, AND THE PARCEL SAYS WHICH IS WHICH. The two dwellings are graded between themselves by the end rule: the crosswalk ranks the two-room frame cottage 1 and the deep-plan frame cottage 3, so the better of the two takes the east end of the run, the end nearer the town's only crossing of the main stem in July 1835. THE STORE IS NOT GRADED BY IT. T-0024 settled that the face rule ranks DWELLINGS and a non-dwelling is placed by its own function, and the function clauses are both satisfied before the run is ordered: a store may not take a light street and this one takes the town's business front, and a commercial roof stands ON the street line rather than at a dwelling's typology setback, which a party-line run does by construction. WHERE ALONG THE RUN IT STANDS IS NOT DECIDED BY ANY COMMITTED RULE, and this parcel does not invent one: the store-residence takes the west end because the two dwellings' own grading fills the east, and the within-run order of a store against a dwelling is recorded here as ARBITRARY rather than dressed as a reading. That it ends up the unit nearest J. H. Kinzie's forwarding store is a consequence of the arithmetic and not a criterion — saying otherwise would be T-A15's refused extension coming back in through the door marked function. THAT A STORE-RESIDENCE MAY STAND SHOULDER TO SHOULDER WITH TWO COTTAGES is the frontage-fabric rule this file already states, read here on a principal street where it binds: South Water is in the committed hierarchy's principal class, so the dwelling families are dealt their party-line row without being ranked off the business front, and the row reads as the one picture of this street draws it. LOT 1 STAYS OPEN and the block is not built out. LOT 2 STOPS BEING RESERVED: the first entry named lots 2, 4 and 6 as frontage its run was dealt and the run stands on lot 6 alone, so the ledger was holding a lot the ground had never taken — corrected in that entry, which keeps lot 4 because its privy is in that lot's yard and gives up lot 2, moving no record. NO ROOF IS ADDED TO THE TOWN: the four come out of `south_plat_beyond_committed_control`, the south district's balance waiting on street control past State and Washington, and every marginal still sums to the programme's total. WHAT IS UNVERIFIED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this lot in July 1835, that there were three of them, that they stood shoulder to shoulder, that one of them was a shop, and that a privy stood in the yard behind them are all inventions of this programme, bounded by the reconstruction spec and graded at the bottom tier in every record it writes. The side lot lines the row crosses between its own units are conjectural; the block face it stands on is not.

open_lots.why: The Lake-and-Clark corner, kept open on the reason the first deal gave it and now measured rather than named: tools/measure_end_rule.py blk_south_water_clark --list puts its frontage 231.87 m walked from the foot of the Dearborn Street drawbridge, the remotest of this block's eight lots from the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835, where lot 6 at the other corner reads 35.15 m. dealt_against_a_request.why: THE ADDITION'S FIRST ROOFS, AND THE REQUEST IS ONLY HALF THE ARGUMENT — THE OTHER HALF IS THE MEMO THAT SAYS HOW FEW OF THEM MAY STAND. Kinzie's Addition had no schedulable ground at all until 2026-09-28: twenty-seven of the North Division's thirty-two platted block rows stood `unsubdivided` because no lot rule had been read for Wright's sheet, so the district's headroom was 0 and nothing could be dealt here however many households wanted a roof. T-1741 read the rules Wright actually draws inside the cells — five clear rules across this block's face, 47.0 ft of lot frontage, `inferred` and recorded as such in `data/traces/kinzie_addition_lot_lines.json` — and cut twelve lots on it. The 665-roof schedule then opened the block with 47 roofs of capacity, 43 of headroom and a committed family mix, and T-1522's placement pass wrote ELEVEN slot requests against it: five D7 houses under `merchant_and_professional_dwellings` on the four corner lots, five D3 cottages and two D4 cottages under `tradesman_dwellings` on the interior. THIS DEAL BUILDS TWO OF THE ELEVEN. The two are the topmost pair of the `tradesman_dwellings` requests on this block in the seating file's own order — hh_baily_john's D3 on lot 8 fronting Indiana Street and hh_bailly_joseph's D3 on lot 9 fronting Illinois Street — and the lots are the request's too, which on a block where every lot is free is not a choice at all: there is nothing to argue a cottage off a free lot onto another free lot. WHY TWO AND NOT ELEVEN, WHICH IS THE ONLY INTERESTING NUMBER HERE. `docs/RESEARCH/1835_north_division_extent_and_infill.md` is the committed reading of what the North Division looked like in July 1835 and it is explicit in both directions: the primary maps establish a substantially larger PLATTED north side and show no buildings on it, so the build must leave 'most legal frontage empty' and 'the outer addition stays visibly speculative rather than being mistaken for an occupied city', with 'at least half the plausible frontage' open on the Kinzie-Michigan interior and scattered roofs beyond it. Eleven roofs on twelve lots is the occupied city that memo refuses. So the binding constraint on this block is not the schedule's headroom and not the seating's demand — it is the memo — and the deal is sized to the memo with the other nine requests left standing as requests. THAT DISAGREEMENT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN TIDIED: the seating pass asks twenty roofs of this addition's two subdivided blocks and the memo will not carry twenty, so the surplus is neither built nor quietly withdrawn — it stays on the owed side of the ledger where the next reader can see the two committed files disagreeing. A REQUEST IS NOT EVIDENCE and neither is a memo's silence: both roofs are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier, on invented positions, with the same reasoning notes as every other roof on this row.

dealt_against_a_request.why: THE BLOCK STOOD EMPTY AND THE SEATING ASKED FOR EVERY ONE OF THESE SEVEN ROOFS. blk_washington_wells is the third block of the plat's last tier to be dealt, the range between Washington Street and Madison Street bounded west by Wells and east by La Salle: the lot ledger reads all eight of its lots `free`, nothing stands on any of them, and every sample of the modelled ground is above datum.
