The Illinois-and-Rush corner, open for the same reason as lot 10. It carries the block's one remaining merchant-and-professional request -- a two-storey frame house, the most substantial thing this block's plan holds -- and standing that on the speculative edge of town before the addition's ordinary cottages are built would invert what the primary maps show. Leaving it open is what keeps this block reading as the tradesmen's interior its family mix makes it.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE ADDITION'S SECOND BLOCK, AND THE FIRST TIME TWO OF ITS CELLS STAND BUILT AT ONCE. The block was entirely empty -- twelve free lots, nothing standing -- and it is dealt two principal roofs and two yard buildings, which leaves ten of its twelve lots open and 16 of the 20 roofs its schedule apportions unbuilt. That is the reading rather than a shortfall: Kinzie's Addition was the speculative north edge of the town in July 1835 and a block built out to its ceiling here would be a claim about 1835 that the primary maps refuse. THE TWO COTTAGES TAKE OPPOSITE FACES ACROSS THE RULED ALLEY, which is the seating's arrangement and not this file's: hh_andrews_davi's one-room cottage stands on lot 8 fronting Indiana Street and hh_anderson_eli_f's on lot 9 fronting Illinois Street, back to back, both graded `none` in the committed street hierarchy -- lines the plat draws and the traffic model gives no through movement. A dwelling is not a shop and the face-value clause that would refuse a quiet street applies to the trade letters, so a household on an untrafficked face at the edge of the addition is the ordinary case here, not the anomalous one. THE SET-OUT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE WOLCOTT BLOCK'S. Its two cottages stand at 6.0 m from Indiana and 5.0 m from Illinois; these stand at 5.5 m and 6.5 m, deeper on the Illinois side where that block is shallower. The north-division memo reads frontage on this side of the river as alternating roof and open yard with no continuous street wall, and two adjacent blocks set out identically would read across Cass Street as one line of houses -- the reading's own refusal, met by moving the number rather than by asserting it is met. THE TWO YARD BUILDINGS ARE THE HUMBLEST TWO IN THE BLOCK'S PLAN, and the block's schedule holds exactly one of each: a privy off the alley behind the Indiana cottage and a woodshed off the alley behind the Illinois one, one apiece, each serving the lot it stands on. Of the stable, the barn, the smokehouse and these two, the privy and the woodshed are the ones a tradesman's household on the edge of town certainly had; the others are ones it might have had, and the choice is argued down rather than up. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this block in 1835, which buildings they were, that they were dwellings, where on their lots they sat and how far back from the street. The lot grid, the block faces, the Addition's alley, the street hierarchy and the ground reading are all committed and none of them moves here; the side lot lines are conjectural, as they are everywhere on this row, and no lot is numbered.

open_lots_taken_since.why: named open by this deal because it had no roof for it; raised by T-1952 as the North Division's one H3 boarding house the plan offers this block, on the Illinois-and-Cass corner. hh_beaubien_john_s's D5 request, which stood here, is re-seated by the placement pass or owed in writing — see the fourth deal's dealt note. The block's reserved open lot is still lot 0 and the Illinois face's alternation still holds: roof on 1, open on 3, roof on 5, open on 7, roof on 9, open on 11.

dealt_against_a_request.why: THE BLOCK STOOD EMPTY AND THE SEATING ASKED FOR EVERY ROOF ON IT. This is the plat's last tier, the range between Washington Street and Madison Street that Thompson draws and July 1835 had barely begun to occupy; the lot ledger reads all eight of this block's lots free, nothing stands on any of them, and the 665-roof schedule apportions the block 21 principal roofs and 6 yard buildings against a capacity of 31. T-1522's placement pass offered the plat to the banded households in the policy's order and found no standing roof of an admitted family free for seven of them, so it wrote a `slot` against this block's own committed plan for each: hh_beddlecome_ash and hh_beaubien_monique a D7 apiece on the Washington corners, hh_benediet_loma an H2 and hh_beech_reuben an H1 between them on the Washington face, and hh_chapman_george, hh_chandler_catherine and hh_chattin_clark a D3 apiece on the Madison face. Every one of the seven is carried in the order book's `slot_blocks` list with blk_washington_franklin named. So neither the count nor the family mix is this file's choice: the seating asks for seven principal roofs and this deal builds seven. THE LOTS ARE THE REQUEST'S TOO, WHICH IS NOT ALWAYS TRUE: which lot a family stands on is ordinarily this file's to author, but on a block where every lot is free there is nothing to argue against, so the seven lots the seating wrote — 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 — are taken as it wrote them, and lot 1 is the one the schedule's own sizing reserves open. THE SEVEN ARE THE WHOLE OF THE BLOCK'S LOT CEILING AND NOT A METRE MORE: `lot_ceiling_principal` is 7 here, one principal roof to a free lot less the open one, and this deal stands at it exactly. The other fourteen principal roofs the schedule apportions this block would have to stand two to a lot along a named frontage run, and a party-wall row on the town's outermost platted tier in July 1835 is a claim about 1835 that nothing supports. THE SEVEN SEATS WERE CORRECTED ON 2026-10-01 (T-1802). The seven first written here were read off the seating when #186's branch was cut, and by the time it merged none of them still asked for this block; the seven above are re-derived against dev's seating of 2026-10-01 by taking this block's deal off and walking the seating chain to its fixpoint, and they ask for exactly the families the deal raised, so the roofs refusal 7 holds back are the same seven and only the request each one records changes. With the deal standing, other households adopt all seven roofs and these seven slot on the Dearborn, Clark and Market blocks (the T-1622 precedence, still open on T-1626). A REQUEST IS NOT EVIDENCE and nothing here grades any higher for having been asked for: all thirteen roofs are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier, on invented positions, with the same reasoning notes as every other roof on this row.

open_lots.why: The Madison-and-Franklin corner, and the lot this deal names as the block's reserved open one. The schedule's own sizing reserves it: principal room is counted over the free lots LESS ONE precisely so a block is never dealt out of its open lot, and with eight free lots this deal may stand on seven and stands on seven. Which lot carries the reservation is arbitrary within the block and this entry does not pretend otherwise; that one is open at all is the programme's assumption of alternating vacancy, and on a tier the town had barely reached in 1835 that assumption is the least of what is being claimed here.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE PLAT'S LAST TIER GETS ITS FIRST FULL BLOCK. blk_washington_clark opened this tier with two cottages on opposite faces; this block is dealt out to its lot ceiling — seven dwellings, one to a lot, with the eighth lot open — which is the first time any block south of Washington Street carries a street of roofs rather than a pair of them. THE TWO FACES ARE READ DIFFERENTLY, AND THE SEATING IS WHAT READS THEM. Washington Street is graded `light` in the committed street hierarchy and Madison `none`, and the placement pass put its four larger households on the Washington face and its three one-room cottages on the Madison one: the two D7 small two-story frame houses on the Washington corners, hh_benediet_loma's H2 merchant-or-professional house and hh_beech_reuben's H1 between them, and the D3 cottages of hh_chapman_george, hh_chandler_catherine and hh_chattin_clark along the quiet side. Standing a cottage on a street the traffic model gives no through movement is not a contradiction — a dwelling is not a shop, and the face-value clause that would refuse it applies to the trade letters only. THE YARD BUILDINGS ARE DEALT BY WHO KEPT THEM, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THIS FILE CHOSE. The block's plan holds six: a stable (A1), a barn or carriage shed (A2), a privy (A3), two woodsheds (A4) and a small utility building (A5). They are assigned up the household scale rather than evenly, because a stable behind a merchant's house is ordinary and a stable behind a one-room cottage is a claim about how that household lived: the carriage shed stands in the H2's yard, the stable behind the H1, the small utility building behind the D7 on the Washington-and-Franklin corner, a woodshed behind the other D7 and behind hh_chapman_george's cottage, and the privy behind hh_chandler_catherine's. ONE HOUSEHOLD IS DEALT NO YARD BUILDING AT ALL, and that is the block's plan binding rather than an omission: six yard buildings were apportioned and seven dwellings are raised, so hh_chattin_clark's cottage on the Madison-and-Wells corner stands in an open yard. The schedule re-derives after this deal with fourteen roofs of headroom still apportioned to the block, so the yard buildings that did not fit here stay in its plan for the deal that comes after — the same accounting blk_washington_clark used for the stable, barn and smokehouse it did not build. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on this block in 1835, which buildings they were, that they were dwellings, where on their lots they sat and how far back from the street. The lot grid, the block faces, the street hierarchy and the ground reading are all committed and none of them moves here; the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural, as they are everywhere on this row, and no lot is numbered.

dealt_against_a_request.why:
THE SECOND DEAL ON KINZIE'S ADDITION'S SECOND BLOCK, AND IT COMPLETES THE ALTERNATION ON BOTH OF ITS FACES. T-1753 stood two one-room cottages here -- lot 8 on the Indiana face, lot 9 on the Illinois face -- and left the other ten lots open with nine of the block's eleven slot requests standing as requests. This deal raises two more, one per face, and after it the Indiana face reads open-open-ROOF-open-ROOF-open across lots 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and the Illinois face reads the same across lots 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Every roof on this block now has empty ground on both sides of it along its own face, which is what `docs/RESEARCH/1835_north_division_extent_and_infill.md` reads off the primary maps for the Wolcott-Kinzie core: frontage that `alternates between roof and open yard`, with `no continuous street wall`. It is also the ceiling that reading imposes here. A fifth principal roof, on either face, must stand on a lot adjoining one already built -- there is no sixth position left that does not -- so the memo carries four roofs on this block and not five, and the remaining seven requests stay requests on the owed side of the ledger.

THE TWO HOUSEHOLDS ARE NOT THE TOPMOST TWO, AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. In the seating file's own order the next two `tradesman_dwellings` requests on this block after the pair T-1753 built are hh_babcock_chas's D3 on lot 7 and hh_bailly_joseph's D3 on lot 6. Both lots sit immediately west of a standing cottage -- 7 beside the roof on 9, 6 beside the roof on 8 -- and the first deal's own entries for those two lots say, in this file, that they are open so that the roof beside them `stands alone on its face`. Building them would retract that sentence and raise the street wall the memo refuses. So the deal takes the next pair down, which is the topmost pair the memo will carry: hh_baily_john's D4 on lot 5 fronting Illinois Street and hh_barber_beta_l's D4 on lot 4 fronting Indiana Street. (The pass re-runs whole behind every deal, so what the seating file says about any one lot is its answer AFTER this deal and not the number frozen here; the requests named above are what it said before it.) The lots are the requests' own -- on a block where every candidate lot is free there is nothing to argue a cottage off its requested lot onto another -- and the two refused requests are neither built nor withdrawn.

THE FAMILY IS NOT THE FAMILY THE FIRST DEAL BUILT, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS THIS BLOCK FROM READING AS A COPY OF THE ONE ACROSS CASS STREET. blk_indiana_north_wolcott's second deal (T-1756) stood two more D3 one-room cottages on ITS lots 4 and 5, so the two blocks now carry roofs on the same four lot positions. The lot positions are not a choice: they are what the memo's alternation leaves once lots 8 and 9 are built and lots 6 and 7 are refused by position. What IS a choice is what stands on them, and the seating asks a two-room cottage here where it asked a one-room cottage there. A D4 carries a wider and deeper footprint band than a D3 (18-24 ft by 22-30 ft against 16-20 ft by 18-24 ft, `1835_building_inventory.json` § `family_bands_ft`), so the two blocks read across Cass Street as different houses on the same rhythm of open ground rather than as one row stamped twice. The rhythm is the plat's; the houses are not.

THE SET-OUT IS A THIRD ONE AGAIN. These two cottages stand at 7.0 m and 4.5 m from their street lines. Neither number appears anywhere else on either of the Addition's built blocks -- the wolcott block carries 6.0/5.0 and 6.5/5.5 and this block's first deal carries 5.5/6.5 -- and the deeper of this pair is on Indiana, which inverts the first deal's relation on this same block. Their lateral offsets are the opposite sign to the first deal's on each face, so neither face carries two roofs on one line. The same memo that forbids a continuous wall forbids a stamped one: two roofs at an identical set-out four lots apart would read as a surveyed row, which is the one thing the 1835 maps do not show on this side of the river. The variation is a typology, not a measurement of these lots.

THE BLOCK'S PLAN HAS NO THIRD PRIVY IN IT, AND THE DEAL DOES NOT INVENT ONE. After T-1753 the schedule's remaining ancillary room on this block is two stables, two barns or carriage sheds and one woodshed; both A3 privies are spent. So the woodshed goes behind the Indiana Street cottage, and the first of the two stables behind the Illinois Street one. The stable is the humblest of what is left rather than the safest thing to claim, and the argument for it is the memo's own reading of this addition: unworn prairie two tiers north of the settled street, both faces graded `none` with no through movement modelled on either, a river to cross to reach the town's stores. A household living there either keeps a horse on its own lot or does not keep one, and a stable is the building that says which. The barns, the second stable and the smokehouse stay in the plan for the roofs that come after them.

A REQUEST IS NOT EVIDENCE and neither is a memo's silence: both roofs are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier, on invented positions, with the same reasoning notes every other roof on this row carries.

NEITHER COTTAGE WAS TAKEN BY THE HOUSEHOLD IT WAS SIZED AGAINST, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN TIDIED -- IT IS THE SECOND TIME IN A DAY. The adoption step runs before the slot step, so both roofs entered the re-run as standing roofs an admitted clause could adopt, and the two households that took them are the very two this deal REFUSED by position: hh_bailly_joseph, whose D3 request stood on lot 6, adopted the cottage on lot 4, and hh_babcock_chas, whose stood on lot 7, adopted the one on lot 5. hh_baily_john and hh_barber_beta_l, the pair the deal was sized against, end the pass holding slots on lots 7 and 6 -- they have swapped places with the two that were declined. The block's seat count is unchanged at eleven and the town's at 177; what moved is two of them from asking to housed (adopted 131 to 133, slots 46 to 44). T-1626 carries the question of whether a roof raised in answer to a slot should be reserved for the household that asked, and nothing here answers it; the same thing happened on the wolcott block under T-1756 and is recorded in its entry above. Neither household is NAMED on its roof: `name_the_keepers_1835.py` refuses both, because a household minted from the post office's letter lists is not evidence that this person kept this house, so the two cottages stay anonymous count-units with an occupant recorded only in the seating.

open_lots.why: The Indiana-and-Cass corner, and still the lot this block reserves open. The schedule's own sizing reserves one -- principal room is counted over the free lots LESS ONE, precisely so a block can never be dealt out of its open lot -- and the first deal named this corner as the reservation. Nothing about this deal moves it. It is also the west end of the Indiana face's alternation, which reads open here before the roof on lot 4, and it faces the wolcott block's own reserved corner across Cass Street, so the street the two blocks share stays open on both sides.

An interior lot on the Indiana face, immediately west of the cottage this deal stands on lot 4, and open for the reason lot 6 was and is: a roof on the adjoining lot is the difference between scattered houses and a built street, and only the first of those is what the 1835 maps carry. The seating asks a D5 cottage here and the request is left standing.

An interior lot on the Illinois face, immediately west of the cottage on lot 5, open for the same reason as lot 2 and with the same effect. The seating asks a D4 two-room cottage here. Lot 2 and lot 3 sit back to back across the Addition's ruled alley, so leaving both open keeps the block's west third open through its whole depth rather than only on one face.

An interior lot on the Indiana face, and after this deal it is the gap BETWEEN two roofs -- the first deal's cottage on lot 8 to its east and this deal's on lot 4 to its west. That is what it is for. The first deal left it open so the roof on lot 8 would stand alone on its face; this deal needs it open for the same sentence read from the other side, and building the D3 the seating asks here would close the alternation on this face in one move. It is the block's most consequential open lot and the request on it is the one this deal most deliberately refuses.

An interior lot on the Illinois face, the gap between the cottage on lot 9 and this deal's on lot 5, and open for exactly the reason lot 6 is. The seating asks hh_babcock_chas's D3 here -- the topmost unbuilt tradesman request on the block -- and it is refused by position rather than by rank: it is the higher of the two requests this deal declined, and it is declined because its lot adjoins a standing roof and the memo will not carry the wall that would make.

The Indiana-and-Rush corner, open because this deal has no roof for it and because Rush Street is the addition's east fringe, which the north-division memo reads as isolated roofs west of the 1834 shore rather than as an addressed corner. The seating asks a D5 cottage on it. It is also the east end of the Indiana face's alternation, which reads open here after the roof on lot 8, and a corner roof is the last thing this block should raise rather than an early one.

The Illinois-and-Rush corner, the last of the block's twelve and open on the plainest reason of all: nothing was dealt to it. It carries the block's one remaining merchant-and-professional request -- a small two-storey frame house, the most substantial thing this block's plan holds -- and standing that on the speculative edge of town before the addition's ordinary cottages are built would invert what the primary maps show. The block's schedule still apportions it part of the 16 roofs beyond the four now standing, and a later deal takes it off this list with its own argument.

blocks.arrangement_note:
EIGHT ROOFS ON TWELVE LOTS ACROSS THE ADDITION'S TWO BUILT BLOCKS, AND FOUR ON THIS ONE. The block stood at two principal roofs and two yard buildings; it stands at four and four, which leaves eight of its twelve lots open and 16 of the 20 roofs its schedule still apportions unbuilt. That ratio is the deal's whole argument and not a shortfall. This is speculative subdivision two tiers north of the settled town: the north-division memo requires `most legal frontage` to stay empty and at least half of the Kinzie-Michigan interior open, and two-thirds of this block's frontage is open after this deal.

THE TWO COTTAGES TAKE OPPOSITE FACES, WHICH IS THE SEATING'S ARRANGEMENT AND NOT THIS FILE'S. Both of the block's faces -- Indiana Street on the north and Illinois Street on the south -- are graded `none` in the committed street hierarchy, unworn prairie with no through movement modelled on either, so the face rule that ranks dwellings by street class has nothing to separate them and did not choose between the two requests. What the pair does is sit diagonally across the block's ruled alley rather than back to back: the Indiana cottage is on lot 4 and the Illinois cottage on lot 5, and the alley between them carries one yard building apiece rather than a facing pair.

THE YARD BUILDINGS ARE ONE A LOT, AS THEY WERE ON THE FIRST DEAL, BUT THEY ARE NOT THE SAME TWO. A woodshed stands off the alley behind the Indiana Street cottage -- the last A4 the block's plan holds -- and a stable off the alley behind the Illinois Street one, the first of its two A1. The privies are gone: the plan held exactly two and the first deal spent both, so this deal takes what is left rather than adding a third. The stable stands on the shallower-set cottage's lot on purpose, where the rear of the lot is deepest; the plan's remaining stable, its two barns and its smokehouse stay unbuilt, because a stable AND a barn AND a smokehouse behind a two-room cottage is a claim about how these households lived that nothing supports.

THE RUSH-PINE FRINGE IS SETTLED IN THE SAME BREATH, AND IT IS SETTLED BY SAYING SO. T-1754 asked for the scattered better houses on that fringe; the 665-roof programme's district deal apportions it NONE. blk_indiana_north_rush, blk_illinois_north_wolcott and blk_illinois_north_rush are each lotted at twelve lots and each read `roofs: 0`, `families: {}`, `standing_roofs: 0`, and every cell east of Rush Street and north of Indiana Street is `unsubdivided` with no lots at all. The north district's whole remaining allocation -- 47 roofs -- is on this block and the wolcott block. So there is nothing scheduled to build on the fringe, `the open ground left honestly open` is what the schedule already says, and the settlement is a statement rather than a parcel. `docs/RESEARCH/1835_north_division_extent_and_infill.md` carries it in prose, where the next reader of that memo will meet it.

WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on these two lots in 1835, which buildings they were, that they were dwellings, where on their lots they sat and how far back from the street. The block faces, the alley line, the street hierarchy and the ground reading are all committed and none of them moves here; the lot lines are T-1741's `inferred` reading of Wright's rules and the side lines within them are this grid's even cut, which is not the same thing and is graded as such; no lot is numbered, because the sheet's lot numerals have never been transcribed.

open_lots_taken_since.why: named open by this deal because it had no roof for it; raised by T-1952 as the North Division's one H3 boarding house the plan offers this block, on the Illinois-and-Cass corner. hh_beaubien_john_s's D5 request, which stood here, is re-seated by the placement pass or owed in writing — see the fourth deal's dealt note. The block's reserved open lot is still lot 0 and the Illinois face's alternation still holds: roof on 1, open on 3, roof on 5, open on 7, roof on 9, open on 11.

open_lots.why: The Indiana-and-Cass corner, and still the lot this block reserves open. The schedule's sizing keeps one free lot open on every block, both earlier deals named this corner as the reservation, and it faces the wolcott block's own reserved corner across Cass Street. This deal raises its house on the OTHER Cass corner precisely so that this one does not move.

An interior lot on the Indiana face, open for the reason both earlier deals gave it: a roof here would stand beside the cottage on lot 4 and raise the street wall the north-division memo refuses. Nothing is dealt to it.

An interior lot on the Illinois face, and after this deal it is the gap BETWEEN the boarding house on lot 1 and the cottage on lot 5. Open so that each of them stands alone on its face, which is the memo's alternation; its standing request stays a request.
An interior lot on the Indiana face, the gap between the cottages on lots 4 and 8, open for the reason the second deal gave it. Nothing is dealt to it.
An interior lot on the Illinois face, the gap between the cottages on lots 5 and 9, open for the reason the second deal gave it. Nothing is dealt to it.
The Indiana-and-Rush corner, open because this deal has no roof for it and Rush Street is the addition's east fringe. Its request stands unbuilt, as before.
The Illinois-and-Rush corner, open for the same reason as lot 10. Its request stands unbuilt, as before.

blocks.arrangement_note:
THE NORTH DIVISION'S ONE BOARDING HOUSE THE PLAN STILL OFFERS, RAISED ON THE ILLINOIS-AND-CASS CORNER WITH A STABLE AND A PRIVY BEHIND IT (T-1952, of T-1810). The order book carries the North's `larger_boarding_houses` cell at eight ordered and seven standing, and the one roof it owes is the H3 the 665-roof schedule apportions to this block: `1835_platted_seats.json` lists it under `plan_left_unclaimed` with the sentence `the plan offers this family and no banded row of this division is admitted by a clause that takes it`. So this house answers the PLAN and not a household. No North banded row is admitted by `lodging_near_the_landings`, the one clause that takes an H3, so no household adopts the roof and its keeper is drawn by the lodgers stage the way every reconstructed house's is; that is stated rather than papered over with a name.

WHY LOT 1 AND NOT LOT 0. Lot 0 is the one lot on the block with no request on it, and it is the obvious place to put a roof nobody asked for — but both earlier deals named it as the block's reserved open lot and argued the choice: it faces the wolcott block's own reserved corner across Cass Street, so the street the two blocks share stays open on both sides. Building there would retract that sentence and still cost a request, because the schedule's sizing (T-1623) keeps one free lot open and the next one would be taken from a requested lot. Lot 1 is the other Cass corner, on the Illinois face — the face toward the river and the landings, which is where the lodging clause puts its houses — and a roof there keeps the Illinois face's alternation exactly: roof on 1, open on 3, roof on 5, open on 7, roof on 9, open on 11. No roof on this block adjoins another along its face after this deal. THE COST IS ONE REQUEST, AND IT IS OWED IN WRITING: hh_beaubien_john_s's D5 cottage request stood on lot 1. The placement pass re-runs behind this deal and either re-seats that household elsewhere or carries it on the owed side of the ledger; the seating file, not this note, says which. A request is not evidence and neither is this choice.

THE HOUSE AND ITS YARD. The house is the form T-1778 and T-1809 built on Washington Street: two storeys of clapboard on the frame_tavern placeholder with the tavern's cues left off, a one-storey kitchen wing behind, its upper windows and stovepipes sized from the beds the lodging model gives it (the record's `reconstruction.capacity` shows the arithmetic). It stands 3.0 m off the Illinois Street line — nearer the street than the cottages' 4.5-7.0 m, because an inn stands to its street, and deeper than the 1.55 m the Washington houses took, because Illinois Street is a speculative addition street and not a town street. A lofted stable and a privy stand off the block alley in its yard, 4-4.5 m in from the alley edge as every yard building of this module stands. THAT MIX IS NOT THE PLAN'S, AND IT IS SAID: the schedule apportions this block's yard as one stable and one barn or carriage shed, sized for the dwellings it expected; the lodging clause's own sentence puts a boarding house `with its stable in the yard behind it` and T-1810 asks for its privy, so the deal spends two of the block's six roofs of ancillary room on a stable and a privy instead, as T-1809 did for the same reason (L326; this deal is L344). WHAT IS INVENTED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a boarding house, a stable or a privy stood on this block in July 1835. All three are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier, on invented positions, with the same reasoning notes every other roof on this row carries.

dealt_against_a_request.why: THE BLOCK'S OWN FIRST DEAL NAMED THESE TWO LOTS OPEN AND SAID WHAT WOULD FILL THEM, AND THIS IS THAT. `open_lots` on the deal of 2026-08-14 wrote lot 7 and lot 9 down as open because that deal had no roof for them, and the seating pass has since asked for both by name: hh_adams_james holds a D7 slot on lot 9 under the merchant-and-professional clause and hh_bennett_h_c a D4 slot on lot 7 under the tradesman clause. Both requests stand in `1835_platted_seats.json` with the sentence this file is answering — "no standing roof of an admitted family was free in this division, and this block's own committed plan still holds a D7 [D4] roof of headroom" — so nothing here chooses which families to build or which lots to build them on. THE TWO ARE THE WHOLE OF WHAT THE SCHEDULE PERMITS, AND THAT IS WHY THE BLOCK IS NOT FINISHED BY THEM. `lot_ceiling_principal` reads 2 on this block and it is `free_lots - 1` — three free lots, less the one the sizing keeps open — so a third principal roof could not be dealt here however much headroom the plan carries, and the plan carries six. Lot 1 on the Clinton face is the lot that stays open, and it stays open by the rule rather than by a judgement of this deal. THE PLAN'S OTHER FOUR PRINCIPAL ROOFS (a D3, a D5, a D6 and an H3) AND THE TWO YARD BUILDINGS BEYOND THESE TWO ARE NOT DEALT and are not lost: they stay in the block's schedule for a later reading of this ground, and no household is asking for them today. WHAT THIS DEAL DOES NOT DO is add a roof to the town. The 665-roof programme's total is fixed; four of its remaining roofs become standing ones and the remainder re-deals over the blocks still open, which is the cascade L270 describes and measures. THE COTTAGE ON LOT 7 IS A D4 BECAUSE THE REQUEST IS. When this deal was first cut (2026-09-29) hh_bennett_h_c's slot on lot 7 asked for a D3, and the seating pass has since re-sized that household to a two-room cottage; the deal was reconciled to the request standing on the day it merged (2026-10-01) rather than to the one it was first written against, because a deal that answers a request nobody is making any more would be choosing the family itself.

open_lots.why: An interior lot on the Clinton face, and after this deal it is the ONE lot this block keeps open — not because nothing was dealt to it, but because the schedule's own sizing reserves one. `lot_ceiling_principal` is `free_lots - 1`, which is 2 here, and the two requests above spend both. The seating asks no slot on lot 1 at all, so no household is refused by its staying open. It also reads as the block's own gap: Clinton is graded `light` in the committed street hierarchy against Canal's `ordinary`, so the plainer face is the one left with a break in it, which is the same ranking the block's first deal argued its four dwellings on and is not a new claim.

blocks.arrangement_note: FOUR ROOFS THAT CLOSE THE CANAL FACE AND LEAVE THE CLINTON FACE WITH ITS GAP. The block stood at ten roofs on nine of its ten lots' worth of ground -- four dwellings and three yard buildings this module dealt in August, and three anonymous roofs from the pre-plat West approaches parcel that were standing before the plat module existed. It stands at fourteen. The two new dwellings are the two the seating pass asked for: a two-storey frame house (D7) on lot 9, the Canal corner, for the Adams household under the merchant-and-professional clause, and a two-room frame cottage (D4) on lot 7 for the Bennett household under the tradesman clause. A privy stands off the alley behind the house and a woodshed off the alley behind the cottage, one to a lot, which is the same yard rule every block deal in this module has used. WITH THEM THE CANAL FACE IS CONTINUOUS -- all five of its lots carry a principal roof -- AND THAT IS A CLAIM, SO IT IS ARGUED RATHER THAN ALLOWED TO HAPPEN. Canal Street is the teamster approach: `data/streets/1835.json` grades it `ordinary` against Clinton's `light`, the West memo reads the Canal and Lake approach as the division's built edge, and the three pre-plat roofs the parcel inherited are themselves on this side. A continuous frontage of five on the approach is what that reading describes. The Clinton face is not continuous and must not become so: lot 1 stays open by the schedule's own sizing, and the West memo's refusal of an occupied city west of the river reaches the plainer face first. THE SET-OUT IS THE BLOCK'S OWN AND IS NOT REDECIDED. Its Canal dwellings already stand 5.0 m and 5.5 m back from the street line; these stand 6.0 m and 4.5 m, inside the same band and continuing the same irregularity, the deeper one the larger house on the corner. Nothing states any of the four numbers -- on this block or on any other -- and they are claimed as reconstruction in docs/LIBERTIES.md. EVERY COORDINATE IS DERIVED, none authored: `tools/generate_block_infill.py` reads the committed lot polygon and this entry's setback and lateral offsets and places the four roofs from those alone. AND THE GAP THIS DEAL MOVES IS THE ONE THING HERE THAT OVERRULES A SENTENCE ALREADY COMMITTED, SO IT IS SAID OUT LOUD. The first deal named lot 7 open for the 665-roof programme's assumption of ALTERNATING VACANCY on a face -- "which of the face's free lots takes the gap is arbitrary once the end rule has ordered the two roofs on it; that there is a gap at all is the assumption" -- and this deal builds on it, so the Canal face has no gap left. The assumption is not abandoned: the block still carries one, on lot 1 of the Clinton face, where the first deal also put one. What moved is WHICH FACE keeps it, and two things decided that. The seating pass asks for both Canal lots BY NAME and asks for nothing on Clinton, so filling Canal and leaving Clinton is the only arrangement that answers every request the pass makes here; and `lot_ceiling_principal` is 2, so the block could not have taken a third roof to keep a gap on both faces even had a household asked. The first deal's own words are why this is a move and not a contradiction -- the gap's POSITION was arbitrary and its EXISTENCE was the claim, and the claim still stands. `open_lots_taken_since` on that deal records both lots with the ticket that took them, so no committed sentence is quietly deleted. FRONTAGE ARGUED ON THE WEST DIVISION'S OWN ARRANGEMENT, SAID IN THE FIELD AND NOT ONLY IN THIS NOTE. Both roofs this deal raises front CANAL, one of the north-south pair the transpose puts the lot columns against, so the argument is made on the arrangement T-1734 re-made and not on the east-west faces it removed. `frontage_argued_on` says so, because tools/generate_plat_lots.py reads that field to decide whether a dealt parcel HOLDS its block back on the South Division module: silence there is not a re-argument, and a second deal that stayed silent would have pulled this block off the transpose its first deal was re-argued onto — ten lots back to eight, and the lot 8 and lot 9 roofs standing on ground the grid no longer cuts.

dealt_against_a_request.why: THE BLOCK'S WHOLE REQUEST, RAISED, WITH THE TWO FACES EXCHANGED BY THE COMMITTED STREET HIERARCHY. The seating file asks two roofs on this block and no more — hh_baxley_j_m's D3 on lot 7 fronting Canal and hh_beaubien_b's D4 on lot 2 fronting Clinton — which is exactly the ceiling the schedule's free-lots-less-one sizing puts on it, so there is no third request to rank and nothing here is refused for being awkward. The deal raises both families and swaps the faces: Canal is `ordinary` and Clinton is `light` in the lot ledger's reading of `data/streets/1835.json`, the D4 two-room cottage outranks the D3 one-room cottage, and the better face therefore takes the better house. That rule is `blk_randolph_clinton`'s, written into this file one block south when T-1734 re-argued it on the transposed cut, and it is applied here rather than quietly inverted. A REQUEST IS NOT EVIDENCE: both roofs are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier, standing on invented positions on conjectural side lot lines, and both carry the reasoning notes every other roof of this programme carries.

open_lots.why: The Clinton column's second lot from Lake Street, plat numeral 3, and the lot this block keeps open. The schedule's own sizing reserves one — principal room is counted over the free lots LESS ONE, precisely so a block can never be dealt out of its open lot — and of the three free lots it is the one the seating asks nothing on, so reserving it refuses no request. It also puts the Clinton column's gap between the standing recon_1835_west_008 roof on the Lake corner and the cottage this deal stands two lots south of it, which is the alternating vacancy the phase-one parcel already assumes.

blocks.arrangement_note:
THE FIRST DEAL ON THE ORIGINAL TOWN'S WEST TIER SINCE THE TRANSPOSE, AND THE FRONTAGE ARGUMENT IS MADE HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME RATHER THAN RE-MADE. `blk_randolph_clinton`, one block south, carried a deal argued face by face against Randolph and Washington and had to re-argue it when T-1734 turned the cut; this block carried no deal at all, so T-1733 transposed it at once and the argument below is the only one it has ever had. `frontage_argued_on` says so in the field rather than in prose anybody has to find. The cut is two columns of five backing onto a north-south alley, every lot fronting Clinton or Canal and none fronting Lake or Randolph, and this block is one of the few where the sheet's own numerals are read at their own positions — 2|1, 3|4, 6|5, 7|8, 10|9, graded `documented` in the lot ledger. The side lot lines within them and the alley between the columns are still conjectural, and they are what every setback below is measured against.

ELEVEN ROOFS ALREADY STOOD HERE AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS THIS RECIPE'S. Seven came from the pre-plat West approaches parcel — recon_1835_west_007, _008, _014, _015, _016, _023 and _024, placed from typed coordinates months before the plat module existed, so no record of theirs names a lot — and four are the West trade ecology the inferred pass seated: inf_artisan_dwelling_west_a on the Canal-and-Lake corner, inf_blacksmith_shop_west on lot 4 of the sheet, inf_teamster_dwelling_west on lot 8 and inf_teamster_stable_west on the Canal-and-Randolph corner. The generator derives which lots all eleven hold from their own committed footprints rather than being told, and refuses a principal roof on any lot they bar. Three lots are free — indices 1, 2 and 7 — and the schedule's own sizing counts principal room over the free lots LESS ONE, so this block's ceiling is two principal roofs and two is what stands here. The headroom of eight is the block's and never a licence to stand a second house on an occupied lot.

THE TWO HOUSEHOLDS ARE THE BLOCK'S WHOLE REQUEST, AND THE FACES ARE EXCHANGED BY THE FACE RULE. `1835_platted_seats.json` holds exactly two slot requests on this block: hh_baxley_j_m's D3 on lot index 7, fronting Canal, and hh_beaubien_b's D4 on lot index 2, fronting Clinton — both under the `tradesman_dwellings` clause, both on free lots, and together they are the two the ceiling admits. The deal builds both families on both lots and exchanges which face each stands on, because the committed street hierarchy ranks the two faces and the two houses the opposite way round from the request. Canal Street is `worn_earth` in `data/streets/1835.json` and reads `ordinary` in the lot ledger; Clinton is `light_worn_earth` and reads `light`. A two-room frame cottage (D4) is the better of the two dwellings and a one-room cottage (D3) the plainer, so the D4 takes the Canal lot and the D3 the Clinton lot. That is the same rule `blk_randolph_clinton`'s re-argument turned on one block south — the better face takes the better house, off the hierarchy and not off a preference — and applying it here rather than taking the requested lots as given is the one place this deal departs from the seating pass. Neither household is refused: both families are raised, both lots are built on, and what moved is which of the two roofs each lot carries. The seating pass re-runs whole behind every deal and its adoption step runs before its slot step, so which household ends up under which of these two roofs is the pass's answer after the deal and not a number this file can freeze; `dealt_against_a_request` below names what it asked for before it.

ONE YARD BUILDING, AND IT IS THE ONE THE BLOCK'S OWN PLAN AND ITS OWN TRADE BOTH ASK FOR. The schedule apportions this block two ancillary roofs and names them: an A1 stable and an A2 barn or carriage shed. The stable is dealt, off the alley behind the Canal-face cottage. Canal Street is the graded approach from the forks and this block is already the town's teamster corner — a teamster's dwelling on lot 8, his stable on the Canal-and-Randolph corner and a blacksmith's shop between them — so a stable in a Canal-face yard is the ordinary yard building on this face and not a flourish. The barn or carriage shed stays in the plan. A barn behind a one-room cottage on a `light` street is a thing that household MIGHT have had, and this deal builds what a household of this kind certainly had; the plan still apportions it, and a later deal takes it with its own argument. So one of the two cottages stands with no yard building at all, which is what a block dealt two outbuildings for two households on different faces has to mean.

THE SET-OUT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE TWIN BLOCK'S. `blk_randolph_clinton` stands its Canal roofs 5.0 m and 5.5 m back and its Clinton roofs 6.0 m and 4.5 m back; these stand at 6.5 m on Canal and 5.25 m on Clinton, with laterals of the opposite sign to their nearest counterpart across Randolph Street. The two blocks share both of their long faces with each other across one street, and two roofs at an identical set-out on the same face of adjoining blocks would read as a surveyed building line — which is the one thing the 1834 survey geometry does not show on this side of the river. The variation is a typology, not a measurement of these lots.

WHAT THE DENSITY READING SAYS ABOUT FILLING THE CANAL COLUMN. `docs/RESEARCH/west_division_infill_1835.md` puts this ground in Zone B — the Canal/Lake mixed approach — and asks for side gaps `mainly inside the specification's 10-35 ft band`, with `larger breaks between yard groups, not a continuous frontage`. After this deal every one of the Canal column's five lots carries a roof, and that is NOT the continuous frontage the memo refuses: the lots are 23.7 m of frontage each and these cottages are a fifth of that, and the gaps are MEASURED off the committed footprints rather than asserted. The Canal cottage's nearest neighbour of any kind is the blacksmith's shop at 11.34 m — 37.2 ft — and the teamster's dwelling at 14.38 m, 47.2 ft; the Clinton cottage's is recon_1835_west_016 at 19.64 m, 64.4 ft. Every one of those is ABOVE the top of the 10-35 ft band, so the face this deal completes is looser than Zone B's own recommendation and not tighter, and the memo's sentence is about how close buildings stand rather than how many lots are spoken for. The Clinton column keeps its open lot.

WHAT IS INVENTED IS EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that any building stood on these two lots in July 1835, which buildings they were, that they were dwellings, which face each took, where on its lot each sat and how far back from the street. The block faces come from the committed street centrelines, the ten lot numerals are read off the sheet, and the ground reading under all three roofs is `dry: every sample stands above datum on the modelled field`. None of that is evidence about these buildings.

frontage.why: T-0024 sends a workshop to its block's better face, and this block's better face is Randolph Street, the ordinary road west out of the town, while every West Division lot fronts the north-south street on the outer side of its column. So the carpenter's or joiner's shop does not stand on a lot frame at all: it stands in a one-lot frontage run on the Randolph face of plat lot 2, against the Des Plaines corner and on the street line, at the 1.5 m margin the plat module allows, because the placement policy's mechanics_streets clause stands a workshop at its street, where a wagon bringing timber or a customer coming out along Randolph meets it first. The run is one lot long and holds one roof; nothing is built shoulder to shoulder here, and the rest of the face stays as open as the recipe's outer edge requires.

open_lots.why: The Des Plaines column's middle lot (plat lot 6), left open between the standing west_046 shed on plat lot 3 and the two-room cottage dealt to plat lot 7, so neither roof on the outer face has a neighbour along its own frontage. The West recipe's outer edge is 'separated by large gaps', and this is the gap.

The Des Plaines column's southern end lot (plat lot 10), at Washington Street, left open because the outer face of the outermost platted block is where the recipe's w5 edge 'terminates in visibly unbuilt wet prairie rather than filling the legal plat'. The lot line continues through prairie; nothing stands on it.

The Jefferson column's second lot (plat lot 4), left open between the standing west_036 roof at the Randolph corner and the cottage dealt to plat lot 5, for the same alternating vacancy every West outer cluster carries: one principal roof every one to three lots, with open ground between.

The Jefferson column's fourth lot (plat lot 8), left open between the two cottages this parcel deals to that face, so the face reads roof, open, roof, open, roof from Randolph to Washington and never as a continuous row. Which free lot takes the gap is an invention; that there is one is the recipe's own zone-C density.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE FIRST PARCEL ON THE WEST DIVISION'S OUTER PLATTED BLOCKS, AND THE DENSITY IT IS DEALT AT IS READ OFF WEST LOTS (T-1783). Until this deal the West grid was withheld from the schedule whole (T-1455), because the only density the schedule had was the Original Town's party-line figure and these are loose outer blocks of 75 3/5 ft lots in two columns on a north-south alley. `tools/reconcile_665.py` now sizes a lot-ruled West block at the density the reviewed West recipe already stands at on its densest lot-ruled block -- six roofs on blk_west_lake_des_plaines's ten lots -- so this ten-lot block has a ceiling of six, two standing (the recipe's west_036 and west_046) and four dealt. The four are what the schedule dealt, in its order: a two-room cottage, a deep-plan cottage, a storey-and-a-half cottage and a carpenter's or joiner's shop. The carpenter stands in a one-lot frontage run on Randolph Street at the Des Plaines corner, the block's better face and the road toward the town, as every non-dwelling takes its block's better face (T-0024); the two-room cottage two lots south of the standing shed on the same face; and the other two cottages on the Jefferson face at plat lots 5 and 9, so each face alternates roof and open ground and the Washington end of the outer face is left as prairie. The set-outs (1.5 m for the shop, 5.5 to 7.0 m for the cottages) and lateral offsets are inventions bounded by the platted block's own lot lines and differ lot to lot so no two read as a surveyed row. Which family stands where, which lots are open, and the setbacks are all reconstructed; the lot lines and the block are the sheet's (plat block 47).

WHY NOT THE CORNERS, which the `lodging_near_the_landings` clause reads as where the documented lodging roofs stood ("on a corner, an approach or the water"). So the pair stands mid-block, and that is a liberty and not a finding. The stable stands off the alley on one side of each lot and the privy on the other, 4-4.5 m in from the alley edge as every yard building of this module stands, and each serves only the lot it is in the yard of. THE YARD MIX IS NOT THE PLAN'S, and it is said: the schedule apportions this block's yard as a mix sized for the dwellings its plan expected, and a stable and a privy apiece is what the documented lodging roofs show, as L326 states for the Clark block. With T-2145's Clark blocks and T-2146's Wells blocks standing, the seating's fixpoint leaves six `slot` requests on blk_school_section_tier_81 with no structure under them: a D5 on lot 2, a D5 on lot 3, a D4 on lot 4, a D4 on lot 5, a D2 on the east Madison corner (lot 6) and a D6 on the east Monroe corner (lot 7). The 665-roof schedule (data/reconstruction/1835_665_roof_programme.json) gives the block `lot_ceiling_principal` 7 over its eight free lots, the eighth being the reserved open one, and its family list is one D2, two D4, two D5, one D6 and one H3, with no yard roof. THE H3 IS NOT BUILT HERE, for the reason T-2146 left block 95's: no household asks for it, because no banded South clause admits the family, and raising a boarding house moves the lodging model that seat_lodgers_1835.py refuses to re-draw without a deliberate re-freeze. Lot 1 is left open for it and the roof stays with T-1957 and the South's other owed boarding houses. So the count, the families and the lots are the seating's and the schedule's, and nothing in this deal chooses them. (The first deal on this branch, against the seating before T-2146 landed, was a D3, a D7 and an A2 in place of the D2 and the D6; T-2146 spent the town's last D3 and D7 against their family targets, and the schedule re-dealt the block.)

open_lots.why: The Madison-and-Market corner, the block's reserved open lot. The schedule's sizing (T-1623) counts principal room over the free lots less one so that a block is never dealt out of its open lot, and `1835_platted_seats.json` keeps this lot clear of every request; which lot carries the reservation is arbitrary within the block, and this entry takes the one the seating already names.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE FIRST HOUSES SOUTH OF MADISON ON MARKET: THE SCHOOL SECTION TIER'S MARKET BLOCK BUILT TO ITS ORDINARY DWELLINGS (T-2147, piece 4 of T-1755). The owner ruled on 2026-10-05 that the South's owed dwellings cross Madison onto the School Section's Madison-Monroe tier, whose lots the state sold one by one in October 1833, and T-2144 put the tier's five dry South blocks on the grid at one principal roof per lot. This deal builds the six houses the seating asks for on block 81, the tier's westernmost South block between Market and the section's eighth line: on the Madison face a larger frame house (D5) on lot 2, a tradesman's frame house (D4) on lot 4 and a small cottage (D2) on the east corner; on the Monroe face a D5 on lot 3, a D4 on lot 5 and a frame house (D6) on the east corner. Lot 0, the Madison-and-Market corner, stays the block's reserved open lot, and lot 1 on the Market corner is held for the schedule's H3 (T-1957). The schedule deals the block no yard roof. Every metre is read off the committed lot polygon by tools/generate_block_infill.py. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that these houses stood on this block in 1835 (the tier was sold, not shown built), where on the lot they sat and how far back; all six are anonymous count-units at the bottom tier toward the schedule's documented aggregate. The lot grid, the block faces, the street hierarchy and the ground reading are committed and none of them moves here.

dealt_against_a_request.why: THE BLOCK'S FOUR REQUESTS, RAISED ON THE LOTS THEY ASKED FOR. Once plat block 50 is on the layer (T-2148: Clinton, Jefferson and Des Plaines carried to Madison, the plat's south town line, as T-2143 carried Canal and West Water), the seating file asks four roofs of it, all on the Canal face: hh_behan_thos's H2 on lot index 5 (the Washington corner) and hh_beaubien_alexandre's H1 on lot index 9 (the Madison corner), both under the merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause, and hh_chark_john_a's D5 on lot index 7 and hh_catran_o_p's D4 on lot index 8 under the tradesman_dwellings clause. The schedule deals the block the rest of the West balance it inherits from west_division_beyond_committed_control -- an H3 boarding house, eight yard buildings and the F3 freight roof -- and the H3 takes the one Canal lot the requests leave, lot index 6. A REQUEST IS NOT EVIDENCE: every roof here is an anonymous count-unit at the bottom tier, standing on an invented position on a conjectural side lot line, and the seating pass re-runs behind the deal to say which household ends up under which roof.

deferred.why: The large river warehouse the West balance carries, and the reason it is not built here is the ground rather than the anonymity, as on blk_lake_franklin. F3's own crosswalk entry makes water access a precondition of the form -- 'Landing apron and cargo-door arrangement must follow site access and cannot extend into water or duplicate a counted pier' -- and this block is bounded by Washington, Madison, Clinton and Canal, four platted streets, a full plat module west of the South Branch with West Water and plat block 51 between it and the bank. tools/reconcile_665.py already HOLDS the roof on the plat for that reason (waterside, T-0316, L203), and tools/generate_block_infill.py refuses F3 by name. The slot is NOT dropped: the roof is still owed in the order book's warehouses_freight/west row, which moves with the rest of the West remainder to the ticket that owns it. SEATED ELSEWHERE BY T-2150 (2026-10-08): the order book's West freight row is now filled by recon_1835_branch_freight_f2_001, an F2 (the family tools/reconcile_665.py deals the West since T-2022 built the town's first F3) on the Washington corner of blk_west_washington_canal's West Water face, the block between this one and the bank, on the placement policy's bank_landing clause (L400). This slot stays deferred because it is this deal's record of what the schedule handed the block and what the ground refused; nothing is owed here any more.

blocks.arrangement_note: THE FIRST ROOFS ON PLAT BLOCK 50, AND THE FOURTH PIECE OF THE WEST DIVISION'S REMAINDER (T-2148). Until T-2148 this block was not on the layer: Clinton stopped at local N -400, the old south edge of the modelled field, and the omission read 'Clinton Street's committed centreline stops 107 m short of this block'. T-2148 carried Clinton, Jefferson and Des Plaines to Madison on their own straight bearings, keeping each old end as a vertex (generate_plat_lots.CARRIED_REACHES), and the block is cut on the Original Town's west tier like blk_randolph_clinton and blk_lake_clinton north of it. It is the first block of that tier the schedule reaches EMPTY, so it takes the Original Town's density (39 roofs of capacity) and with it the West balance that had stood gated beyond the committed control: 14 roofs, of which 13 are built here and the F3 is deferred. The five principal roofs all front Canal, the street the lot ledger reads `ordinary`: an H2 merchant's house on the Washington corner (plat lot 1), an H3 boarding house (plat lot 4), a D5 and a D4 cottage (plat lots 5 and 8) and an H1 house on the Madison corner (plat lot 9). Eight yard buildings -- a stable, three barns or carriage sheds, two woodsheds and two small utility sheds -- stand at the alley ends of those five lots. The whole Clinton face stays open, so the tier reads as the thin western edge of the built town. The set-outs (6.0, 4.5, 7.0, 5.0 and 6.5 m) and lateral offsets are inventions bounded by the lot lines, staggered so the face does not read as a surveyed building line. WHAT IS INVENTED: that any building stood on these lots in July 1835, which buildings they were, which lot each took, where on its lot each sat and how far back from the street. The block faces come from the committed street centrelines and the ten lot numerals are read off the sheet; neither is evidence about these buildings.

A yard building seats nobody, so no household asks for it.

The schedule holds it as reconcile_665.ROW_LOT_GRANTS, a table of one: the lot keeps two row units, its room goes only to an H3, and once the boarding house stands the room is spent.

blocks.arrangement_note: A BOARDING HOUSE BESIDE THE WEDGE'S HOUSE ON LAKE STREET (T-2196, of T-1957). The South owed two large boarding houses that no open block could hold: every one of the 26 open South blocks keeps one free lot and holds one roof per lot otherwise, and only a documented store shares a lot. The owner ruled on 2026-10-09 that lot 7 of the Market wedge, where T-2238 stood a D5, becomes a two-unit party-line row, for this block only. So one H3 stands party-walled to the D5's east side on the Lake Street face, and the second H3 stays owed in the gated balance beyond committed street control until the S9 street work lands. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a boarding house stood here in 1835, that it shared a wall with its neighbour, its size and its keeper. The wedge's lots are themselves reconstructed (L409), and this is an anonymous count-unit toward the schedule's documented aggregate of boarding houses.

redealt.why: THE LAST SIX OF THE 32, AND THE RULING THAT FREED THEM. T-1445 adjudicated the town's anonymous roofs and returned 32 refamily verdicts; T-1451 carried out the six whose ids do not move, T-1494 the phase-one South parcel's eleven and T-1480 the North Division's nine. These six are the platted blocks', and the rename was never what stopped them. Every one is an A-family yard building at a `yard` setback off its block alley, behind the principal roof on its own lot, and the adjudication moves each into an ordinary-dwelling family. The inventory class was read off the family GROUP alone, so each promotion made a SECOND principal roof on an occupied lot and the parcel gate refused all six; T-1482 measured that, costed the three ways out and asked, because all three change what the town is. The owner answered on 2026-09-23: treat a rear cottage as ancillary, so a lot may carry a main house plus a rear dwelling. T-1610 wrote the ruling into the placement policy as `rear_dwelling_behind_its_own_roof` and into `reconcile_665.inventory_class`, which now reads the position as well as the group. THIS IS THE RE-DEAL ITSELF, and it is a re-deal and not a field edit: the slot's family moves and its class is ASKED of that derivation, which `generate_block_infill.check_slot_inventory_classes` then refuses to let disagree. NOTHING IS ADJUDICATED HERE --- every family is the `to_family` T-1445 reached and every reason beside it is T-1445's own, quoted. NO ROOF MOVES: each slot keeps its lot, its setback and its lateral offset, because the adjudication refused these families' placement policy and not their positions. NO FOOTPRINT IS CHOSEN: the block recipe authors no dimensions, so the generator re-samples each one inside its new family's own band. NO CONFIDENCE MOVES: these roofs are reconstructed count-units before and after, and refamilying changes what an invented building is, never how well attested it is. The six record ids move with the family, and every committed file that named one is carried across with them. Recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md.
